- builder: Mid-tier implementer for well-scoped changes with a clear spec: apply a planned edit, write a test from a described behavior, mechanical refactors, doc/report updates. Give it exact files and acceptance criteria. Not for open-ended design or ambiguous debugging - keep those in the orchestrator session.
 (Tools: Read, Grep, Glob, Edit, Write, Bash)
- claude: Catch-all for any task that doesn't fit a more specific agent. FleetView's default when no agent name is typed. (Tools: *)

- claude-code-guide: Use this agent when the user asks questions ("Can Claude...", "Does Claude...", "How do I...") about: (1) Claude Code (the CLI tool) - features, hooks, slash commands, MCP servers, settings, IDE integrations, keyboard shortcuts; (2) Claude Agent SDK - building custom agents; (3) Claude API (formerly Anthropic API) - Messages API for directly passing messages to Claude, Tool Runner (`client.beta.messages.tool_runner`) for running an agentic loop over your own tools, manual tool-use loops, Managed Agents for server-hosted agents with a managed sandbox, prompt caching, and general Anthropic SDK usage; (4) Claude Tag (Claude in Slack) - what it is, setting it up for a Slack workspace, `/install-slack-app`. **IMPORTANT:** Before spawning a new agent, check if there is already a running or recently completed claude-code-guide agent that you can continue via SendMessage. (Tools: Bash, Read, WebFetch, WebSearch)

- Explore: Read-only search agent for broad fan-out searches — when answering means sweeping many files, directories, or naming conventions and you only need the conclusion, not the file dumps. It reads excerpts rather than whole files, so it locates code; it doesn't review or audit it. Specify search breadth: "medium" for moderate exploration, "very thorough" for multiple locations and naming conventions. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)

- general-purpose: General-purpose agent for researching complex questions, searching for code, and executing multi-step tasks. When you are searching for a keyword or file and are not confident that you will find the right match in the first few tries use this agent to perform the search for you. (Tools: *)

- nori-change-documenter: Creates documentation about changes to a codebase. Call the nori-change-documenter whenever you change the codebase. Provide all of the relevance context for *why* the change was made. Be extremely detailed! Provide as much context as possible so the agent can accurately update documentation. (Tools: Read, Grep, Glob, LS, Write, Edit, Bash)

- nori-codebase-analyzer: Analyzes codebase implementation details. Call the nori-codebase-analyzer agent when you need to find detailed information about specific components. As always, the more detailed your request prompt, the better! :) (Tools: Read, Grep, Glob, LS)

- nori-codebase-locator: Locates files, directories, and components relevant to a feature or task. Call `nori-codebase-locator` with human language prompt describing what you're looking for. Basically a "Super Grep/Glob/LS tool" — Use it if you find yourself desiring to use one of these tools more than once. (Tools: Grep, Glob, LS)

- nori-codebase-pattern-finder: nori-codebase-pattern-finder is a useful subagent_type for finding similar implementations, usage examples, or existing patterns that can be modeled after. It will give you concrete code examples based on what you're looking for! It's sorta like nori-codebase-locator, but it will not only tell you the location of files, it will also give you code details! (Tools: Grep, Glob, Read, LS)

- nori-initial-documenter: Creates documentation about a codebase. This agent creates the initial documentation for the codebase; use this agent when you want to create documentation and no existing documentation is present. (Tools: Read, Grep, Glob, LS, Write, Edit, Bash)

- nori-web-search-researcher: Do you find yourself desiring information that you don't quite feel well-trained (confident) on? Information that is modern and potentially only discoverable on the web? Use the nori-web-search-researcher subagent_type today to find any and all answers to your questions! It will research deeply to figure out and attempt to answer your questions! If you aren't immediately satisfied you can get your money back! (Not really - but you can re-run nori-web-search-researcher with an altered prompt in the event you're not satisfied the first time) (Tools: WebSearch, WebFetch, TodoWrite, Read, Grep, Glob, LS)

- Plan: Software architect agent for designing implementation plans. Use this when you need to plan the implementation strategy for a task. Returns step-by-step plans, identifies critical files, and considers architectural trade-offs. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)

- reviewer: High-judgment read-only review. Use to check a diff or design for correctness bugs, edge cases, and simpler alternatives before integrating - especially work produced by builder agents. Returns findings with file:line references and severity; does not fix anything.
 (Tools: Read, Grep, Glob, Bash)

- scout: Cheap, fast read-only recon, executed on GPT-5.6 Terra (medium reasoning) via the Codex CLI. Use for searches, file inventories, "where is X defined/used", summarizing a file or directory, running read-only bd/git commands or tests and reporting output verbatim. No editing. Delegate here whenever the task is mechanical lookup rather than judgment. Prefer calling `scripts/codex-agent scout` directly from the orchestrator when you can (same isolation, no relay hop; include the recon rules from this file in the prompt); this agent type is the interface for workflow agentType calls and the fallback when codex is unavailable.
 (Tools: Read, Grep, Glob, Bash)
- statusline-setup: Use this agent to configure the user's Claude Code status line setting. (Tools: Read, Edit)

- quota-watch: Monitor Amp Free quota and handoff before exhaustion. Use when user says quota-watch, check quota, or monitor usage.
- initialize-noridocs: Initialize docs.md files throughout the codebase
- nori-create-skillset: Create a new custom skillset by cloning an existing skillset
- nori-switch-skillset: Switch between Nori configuration skillsets (amol, senior-swe, product-manager, documenter, none)
- session-close: Cold-start-readiness check before ending a work session - runs the 3 judgment prompts plus the mechanical backstop, then the standard close/push.
- setup-beads-sync: Set up a private GitHub Dolt repo for personal beads and configure sync for the current project
- switch-nori-profile: Switch between Nori configuration profiles (amol, senior-swe, product-manager, documenter, none)
- triage: Layer 2 issue triage - mirror upstream into bd, classify each stub to a one-line disposition, emit a short digest. Never posts text upstream.
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- artifact-design: Design guidance and fundamentals for Artifacts.
- artifact-capabilities: Runtime capabilities a published Artifact page can be granted — behavior static HTML cannot provide on its own, such as the page reading live or connected data, keeping state shared across viewers, or updating and republishing itself. Serves this user's live capability roster and the typed call definitions. Load it whenever the user asks for an artifact needing any such runtime behavior.
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled cloud agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring cloud agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run ("run this once at 3pm", "remind me to check X tomorrow").
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).
- init: Initialize a new CLAUDE.md file with codebase documentation
- review: Review a GitHub pull request; for your working diff use /code-review
- security-review: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch

Drain the tri:claim issue backlog via theme-clustered sweeps
52 open tri:claim issue stubs as of 2026-07-26 with no drain pattern (PR queue has author-clustered sweeps; issues have nothing). Owner asked for a drain strategy this session — strategy doc/decisions to be attached here. Analog of author-clustered-pr-sweeps memory but clustered by subsystem/theme instead of author.
=====
Productionize local-first proxied Dolt mode
Campaign control plane for bringing Beads proxied Dolt mode to production quality without weakening the default managed-local, offline-first topology. Acceptance journey: install → migrate a copy → work offline → concurrent writers → crash/restart recovery → push/pull between machines → backup/restore → doctor → migrate back. The live mybd database remains embedded until disposable and shadow-copy stages pass. Public contributor work stays in upstream issues and pull requests; this epic links existing ownership and creates local children only for apparently unowned gaps.

content.text:
Both are real dents, but they're different kinds of work, and that decides it for me.

## Preference: route the 43 pr-mirror stubs first

Reasons, grounded in what I just looked at:

1. **It feeds proven machinery.** The pr-mirror stubs are mirrored upstream PRs (each carries the PR URL, author, size, and a triage-disposition menu). The PR-review lane already has everything downstream: author-clustered sweeps (owner-endorsed pattern, two reference runs), `pr-preflight`, `pr-handoff`/`pr-babysit` for merge tails, and `pr-close-handoff` for declines. This task is *routing*, not reviewing — mostly mechanical clustering with a well-defined output, which is exactly what orchestrates well.

2. **The server-mode sweep has a coordination hazard the pr-mirror work doesn't.** The 34 `theme:server-mode` stubs overlap the mybd-psxg campaign, whose charter explicitly says it "links existing ownership and creates local children only for apparently unowned gaps." A bulk sweep risks creating duplicate children or stepping on campaign lanes (mybd-uiiu, mybd-6vbo are live patrol tails in that territory). That sweep needs a sequencing decision against psxg's structure first — more in-session judgment, less parallelizable, and honestly a decision with your fingerprints on it, not just mine.

3. **PR stubs decay; issue stubs keep.** Heads move, authors disengage, and some of these 43 are likely already stale — mybd-cazb duplicates the open mybd-2yun deep-review lane for the same rebase work, and several reference PRs from the July sweeps that may already be absorbed. Every week they sit, the routing gets less accurate. The server-mode issues will still be true next month.

## Orchestration sketch (pr-mirror routing, ~200k default budget)

- **Phase 0, inline scout:** refresh upstream state for all 43 PRs in one batched `gh pr list`/GraphQL pull (mind the tri-pull 502 memory — small batches). Fields: state, author, mergeable, last activity, whether already merged/closed/superseded.
- **Phase 1, workflow fan-out (cheap tier, haiku/scout):** one agent per stub or per small batch — cross-check each stub against existing bd lanes (`bd list` search for the PR number) and prior sweep reports, classify: *dead* (PR merged/closed upstream → tri-close), *duplicate* (already has a bd lane → close stub, link), *live* (needs review → keep).
- **Barrier, then cluster:** dedupe genuinely needs the full set — cluster survivors by author, matching the author-clustered-sweep pattern. My guess from the titles is a handful of authors dominate.
- **Phase 2, serial bd mutations in-session:** close the dead/dupe stubs with reasons, create one sweep bead per author cluster under the PR-campaign umbrella (mybd-4vsr or a child of mybd-xmx7), with the stub IDs listed and `discovered-from` links. Validate aggregates before the mutation stage (the null-row lesson from the 52-agent retro).
- **Not in scope:** actually reviewing the 43 PRs. That happens in follow-up author-sweep sessions, one cluster each.

The server-mode sweep I'd stage as its own later session: first a short in-session mapping of the 34 stubs against psxg's existing children and ownership links, then bring you the collision list before creating anything.

On your third point — agreed that 115 `tri:defer` in `bd ready` overstates readiness. That's worth a small bead of its own (either a `defer_until` on those stubs so `bd ready` hides them, or an upstream feature ask if the label-vs-defer distinction can't be expressed today). Want me to file that and start the pr-mirror routing?

113:### #5065 — halaprix: fix(github): include bead metadata in synced issue bodies
119:PR #5065 implements items 1 and 2 of gastownhall/beads#4307: it renders a delimited `<!-- bd-github-sync: start/end -->` block into pushed GitHub issue bodies carrying the bead ID marker plus dependency/dependent tasklists, strips that block on pull so local descriptions stay clean, and wires a new `PushHooks.FormatDescription` for `bd github sync`. The approach is sound and matches the existing Linear precedent (`cmd/bd/linear.go:763` + `internal/linear/mapping.go:26`), scope is disciplined (comment mirroring correctly excluded), and the `CreateIssue` change to use the mapper's title/body is a real latent-bug fix. However the pull-side ID extraction trusts an unvalidated, unscoped marker anywhere in an externally-authored issue body and feeds it straight into the engine's local-ID matching, which can silently overwrite an unrelated local bead; and the hook is wired into only one of the two GitHub push entrypoints, so `bd github push` erases the tasklists that `bd github sync` writes.
121:**Overlap:** Direct conflict with open PR gastownhall/beads#4329 ("fix(github): content-based dedup on push to stop re-PATCHing every issue (#4214)"), which the author acknowledges in the PR body but only as "adjacent". It touches the same three files plus internal/tracker/engine.go, and its `PushFieldsEqual` (`local.Description != remote.Body`) and `PushContentHash(local.Description)` become permanently unequal once #5065 renders a managed block into remote bodies — combining them as-is reintroduces #4214. No other open PR targets #4307 or the marker/tasklist scope (searched open PRs touching internal/github/mapping.go).
127:- **major** — Integration conflict with open PR gastownhall/beads#4329 ("content-based dedup on push", same files: internal/github/mapping.go, internal/github/tracker.go, cmd/bd/github.go). #4329 compares `local.Description != remote.Body` and hashes `local.Description` in `PushContentHash`. Once #5065 renders the sync block into the remote body, local description and remote body can never be equal, so the dedup would never fire and every issue gets re-PATCHed on every push — precisely the bug #4214 that #4329 exists to fix. Additionally the tasklist content depends on dependency edges and on deps acquiring external refs, so a hash over `local.Description` alone is stale even after stripping. Whichever PR lands second must reconcile: compare `RenderGitHubIssueBody(...)` output against `remote.Body`, or strip the block from both sides and hash the dependency set separately.
148:**Overlap:** Sibling PR #5089 (\"make the shared pool's per-I/O read/write deadlines configurable\") also touches internal/storage/dolt/store.go but in disjoint regions (buildServerDSN/config plumbing vs. the two recompute funcs); the PR body's claim of no textual conflict looks correct and both are currently MERGEABLE. #5052 (backup on an undeadlined one-shot connection) is the same class of fix but touches different code. No other open PR touches these recompute paths (#4346 touches blocked-state recompute updated_at in internal/storage, worth a rebase check but no line overlap here).
207:### #5052 — steveyegge: fix(backup): run backup sync/restore on an undeadlined one-shot connection
227:### #5066 — steveyegge: fix(update): refuse overwriting a live foreign claim without --force
235:**Overlap:** Thematic overlap with two open ownership PRs from the same author line: #4697 (feat(ownership): claim_fence + guarded verbs) and #4715 (feat(ownership): holder_token + advisory enforcement mode). Both operate at the storage/schema layer (monotonic fence, holder tokens, --if-fence, claims.enforcement config) while #5066 is a narrow cmd-layer policy fence, so they are complementary rather than duplicative — but if #4697 lands first there will be textual conflicts in cmd/bd/update.go flag registration and internal/validation/issue.go, and its --if-fence guard would need the same skip treatment the fence gives --if-assignee. #5066 is the smaller, self-contained change and should land first. No overlap with recently merged work; the base-branch v1.1.2 hotfix (#5091) does not touch these files.
249:### #5067 — steveyegge: fix(test): prebuild bd for subprocess tests; fit cmd/bd inside the package deadline
270:### #5077 — steveyegge: fix(dolt): recover persisted remotes in the GH#2118 cold-start window
276:PR #5077 extends the existing GH#2118 cold-start evidence rule (an empty `dolt_remotes` on a freshly started sql-server is not proof of "no remote") from the read-only push/sync gate to three mutating call sites, and upgrades it from detection to recovery by exposing the persisted name+URL enumeration (`DoltStore.PersistedRemoteInfos`, with `HasPersistedRemote` derived from it). The approach is right, matches the direction wy-xtv17/wy-82hc5 already set, is well-commented, and lands with focused tests; CI is fully green (all ~50 checks pass) and it merges cleanly against current upstream/main (no drift in the four touched non-test files). One real gap: `bd config apply`'s update leg was not given the same "disk-only remote may be unremovable" tolerance that `ensureDoltRemote` got, so a URL disagreement inside the window now hard-errors where it previously (wrongly, but successfully) applied. The remaining items are minor/nits.
366:**Overlap:** Same author has two adjacent open PRs against internal/storage/dolt/store.go: #5090 (routes recompute-blocked onto the long-timeout connection — addresses the *same* bd-bn8jo incident cited in this PR body, complementary rather than redundant, hunks at ~3438/3470 so no textual conflict) and #5052 (backup on an undeadlined one-shot connection, which refactors execWithLongTimeoutNoTx into a shared `oneShotConn(readTimeout)` helper at the ~1604-1622 region). #5052's hunk is adjacent to 5089's buildServerDSN hunk but does not overlap it; if #5052 lands first, the finding above about clamping the 5m long-timeout downward should be applied inside `oneShotConn` instead of at three call sites. #4473 and #4303 (connection pooling) touch the same subsystem conceptually but not these lines.
376:**Recommendation:** Approve and merge after the author fixes the inverted precedence comment and adds the two rows to docs/reference/configuration.md; the 5m long-timeout clamp can be a follow-up bead (coordinate with #5052's oneShotConn refactor).

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# tri-close — close a bd triage stub AND apply 'triaged' label upstream.
#
# Reads the bd issue's external_ref (gh-pr-NNNN / gh-iss-NNNN) to determine
# which upstream item to label. Aborts if the bd issue lacks a recognized ref.
#
# Usage:
#   tri-close <bd-id>                   # close + label upstream
#   tri-close <bd-id> --reason="..."    # close with reason + label
#   tri-close <bd-id> --skip-label      # close without touching upstream
#   tri-close --dry-run <bd-id>         # show plan, no writes
#
# Idempotent: if the upstream item already has 'triaged', the gh edit is a no-op.

set -euo pipefail
. "$(dirname "$0")/_tri-lib.sh"

UPSTREAM="${TRI_UPSTREAM:-gastownhall/beads}"
BD_ID=""
REASON=""
SKIP_LABEL=0
DRY_RUN=0

while [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; do
  case "$1" in
    --reason=*) REASON="${1#--reason=}"; shift;;
    --reason) REASON="$2"; shift 2;;
    --skip-label) SKIP_LABEL=1; shift;;
    --dry-run) DRY_RUN=1; shift;;
    -h|--help) sed -n '2,14p' "$0" | sed 's/^# \{0,1\}//'; exit 0;;
    -*) echo "tri-close: unknown flag: $1" >&2; exit 2;;
    *)
      if [[ -n "$BD_ID" ]]; then
        echo "tri-close: only one bd-id allowed (got '$BD_ID' and '$1')" >&2
        exit 2
      fi
      BD_ID="$1"; shift;;
  esac
done

Defer issues to put them on ice for later.

Deferred issues are deliberately set aside - not blocked by anything specific,
just postponed for future consideration. Unlike blocked issues, there's no
dependency keeping them from being worked. Unlike closed issues, they will
be revisited.

Deferred issues don't show in 'bd ready' but remain visible in 'bd list'.

Examples:
  bd defer bd-abc                  # Defer a single issue (status-based)
  bd defer bd-abc --until=tomorrow # Defer until specific time
  bd defer bd-abc --reason="waiting on API access"
  bd defer bd-abc bd-def           # Defer multiple issues

Usage:
  bd defer [id...] [flags]

Flags:
  -h, --help            help for defer
      --reason string   Record why this issue is being deferred (appended to notes)
      --until string    Defer until specific time (e.g., +1h, tomorrow, next monday)

Global Flags:
      --actor string              Actor name for audit trail (default: $BEADS_ACTOR, git user.name, $USER)

      --dolt-auto-commit string   Dolt auto-commit policy (off|on|batch). 'on': commit after each write. 'batch': defer commits to bd dolt commit; uncommitted changes persist in the working set until then. SIGTERM/SIGHUP flush pending batch commits. Default: off. Override via config key dolt.auto-commit

      --ignore-schema-skew        Proceed despite forward schema drift (some queries may fail)

---
description: Layer 2 issue triage - mirror upstream into bd, classify each stub to a one-line disposition, emit a short digest. Never posts text upstream.
allowed-tools: Bash(*), Read(*), Grep(*), Glob(*), Agent(*)
---

Run the pinned triage procedure. The deliverable of triage is a DISPOSITION
per item plus one sentence of why - not an essay. This command exists because
free-form triage drowned readers in text (owner feedback, 2026-07-07). Follow
the procedure and the caps exactly; do not improvise extra output.

Hard rules, non-negotiable:

- **Never post text to upstream GitHub.** No `gh pr review`, `gh pr comment`,
  `gh issue comment`. Do not run `tri-submit`. The only upstream writes allowed
  are text-free `triaged` labels via `scripts/tri-close`.
- Run all bd/gh-writing steps **serially** (embedded-Dolt locking).
- Classification subagents are **read-only** and cheap (scout tier).

## 1. Mechanical sync (Layer 1)

```bash
scripts/tri-pull          # mirror new untriaged upstream items into bd
scripts/tri-sync          # close stubs whose upstream item is terminal
```

Record the counts they report for the digest header. If either fails on gh
auth or rate limits, report and stop.

## 2. Classify (Layer 2)

Build the worklist: open bd stubs with a `gh-(pr|iss)-NNNN` external_ref that
are either unclassified (no `tri:*` label) or flagged `tri:stale` by the
tri-drift patrol (upstream moved since classification — reclassify them):

```bash
bd list --status=open --limit 0 --json \
  | jq -r '.[] | select(.external_ref != null and (.external_ref | test("^gh-(pr|iss)-[0-9]+$")))
           | select((((.labels // []) | map(startswith("tri:")) | any) | not)
                    or ((.labels // []) | index("tri:stale")))
           | "\(.id) \(.external_ref) \(.title)"'
```

For each item, produce a classification with EXACTLY this shape (read-only
scout subagents may fetch `gh pr view` / `gh issue view` for signals; batch
several items per subagent):

- `disposition`: one of `close` | `defer` | `claim` | `human` | `needs-info`
- `priority`: P0-P4
- `reason`: **max 200 characters**, one sentence
- `confidence`: high | medium | low

Disposition guide: `close` = obsolete, duplicate, already-handled upstream,
or clearly not actionable by us; `defer` = real but not now; `claim` = we
should do it and the spec is clear; `human` = judgment call the owner must
make (contentious, social, or high-stakes); `needs-info` = cannot classify
from available signals.

## 3. Record (serial)

For each classified item, one bd update:

```bash
bd update <id> --add-label "tri:<disposition>" --priority <Pn> \
  --append-notes "[triage $(date -u +%Y-%m-%d)] <reason>"
```

For `tri:stale` items being reclassified, also remove the stale flag (and the
old `tri:*` disposition label if it changed):

```bash
bd update <id> --remove-label tri:stale
```

For `close` dispositions with **high** confidence only, also run
`scripts/tri-close <id> --reason="<reason>"` (closes the stub and applies the
text-free upstream `triaged` label). Medium/low confidence closes stay open
with the `tri:close` label for the owner to confirm.

## 4. Digest (the only human-facing output)

Write `reports/triage/YYYY-MM-DD.md` (md only, no html). Format, strictly:

```markdown
# Triage digest - YYYY-MM-DD

Pulled N new, auto-closed M terminal, classified K.

| bd | ref | disp | P | conf | reason (<=200 chars) |
|----|-----|------|---|------|----------------------|
```

One row per item, one line per row. After the table, at most two short
sections:

- **Flagged for human** - the `human` and low-confidence items, one line each,
  with the single question the owner must answer.
- **Coverage** - anything skipped (rate limits, fetch failures, window
  truncation reported by tri-pull).

The whole digest must stay under ~80 lines. If the item count would exceed
that, keep the flagged items as rows and collapse the rest into per-disposition
counts, noting the collapse in Coverage.

## 5. Report back

In the conversation, give ONLY: the counts line, the flagged-for-human items,
and the digest path. Do not restate the table. Do not close this command's
work with a session push unless the user asks; the digest file plus bd labels
are the deliverable.

export const meta = {

  description: 'Re-review 6 dormant single-PR-author PRs; draft real dispositions',
  phases: [
    { title: 'Review', detail: '5 author-clustered reviewer agents' },
  ],
}

const REVIEW = {
  type: 'object', additionalProperties: false, required: ['prs'],
  properties: { prs: { type: 'array', items: {
    type: 'object', additionalProperties: false,
    required: ['number','author','verdict','summary','draft_comment','merge_readiness'],
    properties: {
      number: { type: 'integer' },
      author: { type: 'string' },
      verdict: { type: 'string', enum: ['approve','approve-with-nits','needs-changes','decline','already-absorbed'] },
      summary: { type: 'string', description: '3-6 sentences: what the PR does, correctness assessment, overlap/prior-art findings, key evidence file:line' },
      draft_comment: { type: 'string', description: 'ready-to-post GitHub review comment in Markdown: substantive, kind, specific; references code as file:line; no signature line (added at post time)' },
      merge_readiness: { type: 'string', enum: ['merge-when-green','needs-author-action','needs-maintainer-rework','close-after-grace','blocked-on-decision'] },
      rebase_needed: { type: 'boolean' },
      overlap: { type: 'string', description: 'open PRs/issues touching the same surface; empty if none found' },
    } } } },
}

const CLUSTERS = [
  { author: 'fengning-starsend', prs: [4175], hint: 'bd-91bzp: make issue prefix mutations explicit' },
  { author: 'realies', prs: [4288, 4348], hint: 'empty-DOLT_COMMIT suppression pair — review together, likely one supersedes or complements the other' },
  { author: 'ksletmoe-aws', prs: [4346], hint: 'UTC updated_at in blocked-state recompute; check overlap with open PR 4730 (jakelindsay87, same UTC-normalization theme) and with merged fix mybd-2n6g referenced work' },
  { author: 'aaronlippold', prs: [4383], hint: 'config-table commits in server mode (GH#4078); note upstream issue 4078 stub was closed today in favor of this PR — this review decides its fate' },
  { author: 'griels', prs: [4413], hint: 'bd schema command emitting JSON Schema for --json/export output; check drift vs current output shapes and CLI docs conventions' },
]

const results = await parallel(CLUSTERS.map(c => () =>
  agent(`Maintainer re-review for gastownhall/beads (local clone /var/home/matt/dev/mybd/bd-main, ref upstream/main = c989b6b87 freshly fetched). READ-ONLY: no edits, no bd commands, no posting to GitHub — output only.

Context: these PRs are 'dormant sweep residue' — each was answered at most once (mid-June or 2026-07-05) and the author has heard nothing since. Maintainer policy (PR_MAINTAINER_GUIDELINES.md in /var/home/matt/dev/mybd — read it first, especially the prior-art pass and absorb/transform preferences): maximize contributor value, absorb when practical, preserve attribution, request-changes as last resort.

Author: ${c.author}. PR(s): ${c.prs.join(', ')}. Hint: ${c.hint}

For each PR:
1. 'gh pr view N --repo gastownhall/beads --comments' and 'gh pr diff N --repo gastownhall/beads' (fetch once, read locally).
2. Read the touched code at upstream/main via git -C /var/home/matt/dev/mybd/bd-main (the PR may be stale vs main — check whether main has moved under it, whether the problem still exists, whether the change was already absorbed by other commits).
3. Prior-art pass: search for open PRs/issues touching the same files or problem ('gh pr list/search', git log on the touched paths).
4. Produce the schema output. draft_comment must be a real maintainer review a human could post as-is: acknowledge the wait if long, state the disposition plainly, give specific actionable items with file:line, and say what happens next (merge path, rework offer, or graceful decline with reason).`,
    { label: `review:${c.author}`, phase: 'Review', schema: REVIEW })))

const flat = results.filter(Boolean).flatMap(r => Array.isArray(r.prs) ? r.prs : [])
log(`reviewed ${flat.length}/6 PRs`)
if (flat.length < 6) log('WARNING: some PRs missing — list and retry at higher tier')
return { prs: flat }

content.content:
1	Following up on the review from July 5 — apologies that this then sat another three weeks without a resolution; that's on us, not you.
2	
3	To restate the situation plainly: your root-cause analysis here was exactly right, and it *predates* the fix that landed on main. Commit `03cdc6c86` (merged 2026-06-11) modified the same five UPDATE templates you identified — the mark/unmark templates in `internal/storage/issueops/blocked_state.go` (now lines 179, 223, 285, 329 on main) and the direct-blocking fast path in `internal/storage/issueops/dependencies.go` (lines 373, 388) — but took a different approach: `updated_at = updated_at` self-assignment, which suppresses `ON UPDATE CURRENT_TIMESTAMP` without stamping any new value. That choice was deliberate: stamping a fresh timestamp (even a correctly-UTC one) on a derived-state `is_blocked` flip makes independent clones diverge on `updated_at` for the same converged row, and `issues` isn't in the merge auto-resolve allowlist, so every sync surfaces an operator-level conflict. Main's regression tests (`blocked_merge_test.go`) now assert `updated_at` must *not* change on these paths — the inverse of what this PR's tests assert — so the two designs can't coexist and a rebase wouldn't be a mechanical fix.
4	
5	Given that, we're closing this PR rather than asking you to rework it. The value you contributed is real and we want it recorded: (1) we'll close #4298 with a pointer to `03cdc6c86` and credit your diagnosis, which nailed the mechanism (embedded Dolt's `SetQueryTime(time.Now())` inheriting `time.Local`) two days before the fix landed; (2) the broader driver-clock concern — local time leaking into *other* persisted timestamps — is live in open PR gastownhall/beads#4730, which normalizes create-path audit timestamps in `dependencies.go`; if you'd like to weigh in there or cut a narrow follow-up against current main for any path still affected, we'd welcome it.
6	
7	This will stay open for a few days in case you'd like to respond before the close. Thanks again for a genuinely well-diagnosed report and patch — the outcome here is a timing collision, not a quality problem.

1	First: apologies, both for the six-week silence and for the only reply you did get — that June comment asking for a "reproduction recipe" was a triage template mis-fired at a feature PR, and it must have read as nobody having looked at this at all. Someone has now, properly.
2	
3	This is a good idea, well executed. Reflecting the schema from the same `internal/types` structs bd serializes — and driving the enums from the same `All*` lists `IsValid` consults — is the right way to kill the drift problem, and we have live evidence you're solving a real one: open issue gastownhall/beads#5058 is precisely a hand-maintained `json-schema.md` disagreeing with actual `--json` output. The `schemaDocument()` split for DB-free unit testing and the behavior-preserving `IsValid` refactor are both exactly how I'd want this built. I checked your `All*` lists against current main's constant blocks (internal/types/types.go:414-420, 611-622, 912-942) and they still match one-for-one, `TypeEvent` exclusion included.
4	
5	**Disposition: accept.** The PR shows as conflicting, but none of the conflicts are your code's fault — the docs infrastructure moved underneath you after you opened this:
6	
7	- The Docusaurus `website/` tree was deleted entirely in the Mintlify migration (52aea3f7e), so the `website/docs/`, `website/static/llms-full.txt`, and `website/versioned_docs/` edits just get dropped.
8	- `docs/CLI_REFERENCE.md` and `docs/cli-reference/` are now generated from the *released* bd version pinned in `docs/cli-docs.pin` (currently v1.1.0; see d2f87d50d), so new-command docs land via the release-time regen, not hand-edits in the feature PR. Those hunks get dropped too.
9	- `go.mod`: `invopop/jsonschema` is now v0.14.0 (indirect) on main, so the promotion to a direct dep needs a version bump.
10	
11	Per our maintainer policy, that rebase is our work, not yours — I'll take it unless you'd rather do it yourself (say the word and it's yours). Two small nits I'll fold in while I'm there, or you can if you pick it up:
12	
13	- `cmd/bd/schema.go:46` — `outputJSONRaw` returns an error that the `Run` func discards; worth handling for errcheck hygiene (see how cmd/bd/dolt.go:450 treats it).
14	- `internal/types/types.go` — the inserted `AllIssueTypes` var splits the `IsValid` doc comment (the `// IsValid checks if the issue type is a core work type.` line ends up orphaned above the var block); a one-line reshuffle fixes godoc.
15	
16	Your listed follow-ups (memory export record, mirroring the assertion into `cmd/bd/protocol`) are welcome as separate PRs once this lands. Next step: I'll rebase onto current main with the doc hunks dropped, re-run the tests, and take it to merge with your authorship preserved. Thanks for building this — and for your patience with a queue that didn't deserve it.

1	This is an exemplary bug report wrapped in a PR — the captured query trail showing the second `DOLT_ADD ×6; DOLT_COMMIT` after the real commit, the observation that the comment at the `len(tables)==0` early-return already *claimed* to exclude dolt_ignore'd tables while the query never did, and the before/after production numbers make the root cause undeniable. Thank you, and apologies both for the long wait and for the June comment asking for a repro recipe when your body already had a traced root cause and a live-validation table; that reply missed the mark.
2	
3	**Disposition: we want both fixes; the second needs adapting to code that moved under you.** Verified against current main (c989b6b87):
4	
5	1. **The store.go fix is still needed and re-targets cleanly.** `Commit` was refactored into `commitWorkingSet` with config-staging modes, but the dolt_status scan is still unfiltered (internal/storage/dolt/store.go:2385), so the ignored-table flood you traced is fully intact. Your exact predicate already exists on main in `CommitPending` (store.go:2582), which makes this an easy, precedented port. One interaction to preserve: with the filter, the empty-tables path fires more often, and in `configIncludeAll` mode that path deliberately routes to `concludeOpenMerge` (store.go:2423) — your change is compatible with that; just keep it intact.
6	2. **The uow fix needs rework — not because you were wrong, but because main moved.** `doltServerTx.Commit` was rewritten (commit 794ff0790) so a failed `DOLT_COMMIT` rolls back before releasing the pinned connection — returning a session with an open transaction to the pool was itself a bug. Your `!pending -> return nil` skip would release the connection with the `START TRANSACTION` still open, reintroducing that. The guard is still right; the skip path just needs to close the SQL transaction (plain `COMMIT` or rollback) before release. Separately, I'd drop the belt-and-suspenders swallow of nothing-to-commit inside `Commit`: `RunTx` already swallows it at the call site (internal/storage/uow/tx.go:63), and the uow layer deliberately lets that error surface as a lost-update signal (see internal/storage/uow/errors.go and lostupdate_dolt_test.go) — swallowing it one layer down could mask a silently lost write.
7	
8	Rebasing onto moved main is maintainer work under our current policy, and the doltServerTx integration is the fiddly part. Want to take the re-port yourself with the notes above, or shall we do it on our side with your commits and attribution preserved? Together with 4288 (which covers the selective-staging `-m` helpers this PR doesn't), both are headed for merge.
